claim: >-
  The accepted architecture permits only a manifest-bound, non-publishable
  private Core using owned primitives and a normalized semantic seam. Public
  names, production dependency adapters, package carriers, trusted/raw carrier
  exposure, and duplicate binding-record behavior remain gated by ADR-0009,
  ADR-0010, ADR-0012, ADR-0013, and ADR-0014 respectively. The intended
  separation follows dependency inversion, but the exact checkout does not
  enforce the private package boundary independently of active open decisions,
  and its M1 inbound interface is contradictory.

findings:
  - severity: P1
    location: >-
      research/implementation-readiness/report.md:599-601;
      architecture/checks/feature-module-standard-profile.mjs:122-169;
      architecture/checks/governance.mjs:178-201;
      architecture/checks/governance.mjs:673-707;
      architecture/checks/production-artifacts.mjs:107-140
    reproduction: >-
      The report says first-production admission checks accepted private package
      identities, private status, and publication fields independently of active
      blockers. At the exact SHA, validateFirstProductionPackageAdmission has no
      package-manifest argument and performs none of those checks.
      validateBlockedImplementation is the only shown caller of
      productionArtifactsBlockedByOpenDecisions, and line 185 returns immediately
      when blockerIds.size is zero. Therefore, after OD-004 through OD-006 are
      resolved, the exact gate does not read package manifests before accepting
      the inventory. This contradicts accepted ADR-0003's exact package identities,
      ADR-0015's private-package restriction, and the report's remediation claim.
    minimalCorrection: >-
      Add an always-on package-admission validator, independent of the active
      open-decision count. Require a direct package-root manifest for every
      production package, enforce accepted identities, private true, and no
      publication fields during source admission, and add negative tests using
      an empty blocker set, an unknown identity, a missing manifest, and each
      publication field. A later publication transition must require the
      corresponding accepted naming and carrier authorities rather than merely
      an empty open-decision set.
    productOwnerDecisionRequired: false
  - severity: P1
    location: >-
      docs/decisions/0006-clarify-v1-compiler-normalization-and-entry-points.md:33-74;
      docs/open-decisions/OD-005-raw-input-carrier-semantics.md:98-104;
      docs/architecture/mvp-implementation-roadmap.md:90-123;
      docs/architecture/mvp-implementation-roadmap.md:497-522;
      docs/architecture/mvp-implementation-roadmap.md:594-600;
      docs/architecture/self-composition-implementation-guide.md:448-474
    reproduction: >-
      Accepted ADR-0006 defines compileCompositionV1 as the public trusted-object
      entry point, including caller-value admission and snapshot-before-await.
      The M1 export matrix and self-composition guide say the private subject
      exposes that entry point and executes object vectors. In contrast, the
      Phase 3 and Phase 4 text says M1 invokes only a private normalized-value
      seam, is not either JavaScript carrier, and uses the public compiler
      boundary only after both carrier boundaries are accepted. OD-005 says
      candidate object/raw entrypoints before acceptance exist solely for
      qualification and are not production entrypoints. These instructions do
      not identify whether object admission belongs to M1, a qualification-only
      adapter, or the later accepted carrier boundary.
    minimalCorrection: >-
      Publish one consistent M1 interface rule. Prefer a separately named,
      private normalized-value application seam owned by Core semantics, with
      any qualification-only object adapter outside the production source and
      explicitly excluded from carrier evidence. Remove compileCompositionV1
      from the M1 row and stage0 re-export until the trusted-object boundary is
      accepted, or accept a successor that explicitly authorizes the exact
      object-admission subset. Update the roadmap, current-contract guide, and
      self-composition guide together.
    productOwnerDecisionRequired: false
